I've not really told many people this, one girlfriend once who said I was crazy. But I can read people. Not like read their thoughts, but read their emotions, and feelings. Once I get to know someone a little, it's very easy for me to link all the pieces together. What this ends up meaning is that in my close relationships I often know people better than they know themselves. My current girlfriend appreciates this, because in a way it's free therapy, but for me it sucks. I wish that I had someone like me around. Most people that I interact with are shallow, and self serving, and when you can see it on them, it really makes it hard to want to maintain relationships, and the truth is I don't want to maintain them.

As much as I would like to know someone like me, I also don't. Because I'm aware of how much I know, I wouldn't someone who knew that much about me. I feel a little like I'm violating the privacy of people close to me, perhaps it's because I'm not upfront with how much I know.

I didn't really know I was this way until I went to therapy when I was 18. I knew I was different, but I didn't know why. Then all through college I was aware of it, but didn't really understand it. Then the tv show "Lie to Me" came out, and this was the first glimpse I had of other people like me, although my ability is not black and white like it is in that show, and I'm not really a lie detector, more of an emotion detector/reader. It's hard for people to be around me as well, as nothing really gets by me. It's hard to be in a relationship with me because I'm just to aware, and I'm not trying to be. I've learned to keep so much more to myself and let people have their privacy, but it's not really privacy because I still know. Now I just don't act on it, or say anything about it unless it's beneficial. I guess this is my burden.
